wins.text: Running grew mid-single digits in Q3, with Vomero 18 launching across 1,800+ doors and Peg Premium seed pairs nearly selling out in North America; plans to double Vomero 18 distribution by mid-April
Vomero 5 doubled its revenue in Q3; Nike Shox grew revenue by over 10x in the last 3 quarters, signaling early sportswear diversification traction
24/7 apparel collection first-month sales exceeded expectations with capacity being ramped up to meet demand
NIKE Digital North America reduced promotional days from 30+ in Jan-Feb 2024 to zero in Jan-Feb 2025, resulting in several percentage point improvement in full-price demand
Demand creation expenses grew high single digits (~8%) YoY, driving outsized brand impact at Super Bowl and NBA All-Star Weekend; NIKE San Francisco flagship had its best commercial day in 10 years

risks.text: Total revenues declined 9% reported / 7% currency-neutral in Q3; double-digit declines in January and February following a strong December holiday period
Gross margins declined 330 bps to 41.5% due to higher markdowns on NIKE Direct, higher wholesale discounts, inventory obsolescence, product costs, and channel mix headwinds
Greater China revenue declined 15% with wholesale down 18% and EBIT down 42%; traffic declined double digits and retail sales underperformed plan amid aggressive competitive and promotional dynamics
Q4 revenue guided down mid-teens range with gross margins expected down 400-500 bps; digital traffic expected down double digits in fiscal '26 as NIKE repositions its digital business

Inventory remains elevated across all geographies; Air Jordan 1 and Dunk inventory still elevated with continued liquidation actions required through H1 fiscal '26; newly implemented tariffs on imports from China and Mexico creating additional margin headwinds

guidance_items.detail: Q4 revenues expected down mid-teens range (low end), including several points of unfavorable shipment timing in North America and ~2 points of FX headwind; digital traffic expected down double digits in FY26
Q4 gross margins expected down ~400-500 bps, including restructuring charges in prior year and estimated impact from new tariffs on imports from China and Mexico
Q4 SG&A dollars expected up low to mid-single digits, including prior-year restructuring charges; other income/expense (net interest income) expected $45M-$55M for Q4
Full-year effective tax rate expected in mid-teens range; second half plan described as in line with prior quarter communication with shifts between Q3 and Q4

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Timeline for classic shoe inventory cleanup in wholesale vs. direct channels specifically
Long-term structural wholesale margin levels given current discount investments
Geographic progress ranking — which regions are furthest along vs. lagging in Win Now execution
